article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Zoap × Y Life
Breeder: Wizard Trees
THC Content: 20–29%
CBD Content: 0.1–0.2%
Terpene Profile: Beta-caryophyllene , limonene , linalool
Primary Flavors: Sweet candy, creamy sherbet, apple
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Dark Matter is an appropriate name for a cannabis cultivar that seems to become more complicated the closer you examine it. From a distance, the flower fits comfortably into the modern California exotic category: dark coloration, thick resin, tight buds, and obvious candy genetics. Once the jar opens, however, the profile becomes harder to classify. Sweet sherbet and creamy fruit sit beside floral perfume, apple-like brightness, pepper, earth, and a persistent layer of gas.

Wizard Trees created this version by crossing Zoap with Y Life, and the breeder describes it as an evolution of the creamy, gassy candy-sherb direction that helped define its modern genetics. The high develops with similar depth, beginning as a noticeable cerebral shift before a denser physical calm takes over later in the experience. Current Wizard Trees flower has tested anywhere from roughly 20% to nearly 29% THC, placing this weed comfortably in the high-potency category while leaving considerable room for batch-to-batch variation.
Genetics and Lineage

The Dark Matter covered here is the Wizard Trees cultivar bred from Zoap × Y Life. Wizard Trees lists that exact lineage on its official strain page and describes the cross as combining the recognizable terpene character of both families into a deeper interpretation of the brand’s sweet-and-gas style. This clarification is particularly important because Dark Matter is not a unique cannabis name. Older cultivars from Kingdom Organic Seeds and North Genetics also use it but have completely unrelated genetics. When discussing current Wizard Trees flower, Zoap × Y Life is the relevant pedigree.

Zoap supplies much of the perfume, candy, cream, and sherbet character. Its family is closely associated with the modern RS11 / Zkittlez -influenced flavor spectrum, where floral sweetness and unusual soap-like aromatics coexist with fruit and gas. Y Life pushes the cross in a darker direction, contributing fuel, structure, and additional depth. The result feels less sugary than many contemporary candy weed strains even though sweetness remains central to the aroma. Wizard Trees has since demonstrated confidence in Dark Matter as breeding material by using it as a parent in Potion, a Dark Matter × Black Magic hybrid.
Effects and Experience

The beginning of the experience is more cerebral than the dark, resin-heavy flowers might suggest. A moderate amount can produce a distinct head change accompanied by brighter mood, increased interest in music or conversation, and a creative quality that feels engaged rather than frantic. Wizard Trees specifically characterizes the cultivar around nighttime use, creativity, sweetness, gas, and a pronounced head high. The mental component can remain surprisingly articulate during the early stages, which gives the cultivar more dimension than weed that immediately produces heavy sedation.

That balance changes with time. Physical relaxation gradually becomes stronger, creating a heavier feeling through the limbs while the initial mental lift settles into a slower rhythm. Current batches demonstrate why dosage matters. Wizard Trees flower has appeared around 20.3%, 24.7%, 25.7%, 26.2%, and as high as roughly 28.8% THC depending on market and harvest. For experienced cannabis consumers, the progression can feel pleasantly layered. Someone with limited THC tolerance may instead find a large dose disorienting or overly sedating, with possible dry mouth, red eyes, dizziness, anxiety, or impaired coordination.
Medical Benefits

Medical marijuana consumers may gravitate toward Dark Matter when they want strong relaxation without sacrificing the initial sense of mental engagement. The combination of mood elevation followed by heavier body calm may be useful for consumers attempting to temporarily manage everyday stress, physical tension, difficulty unwinding, or restlessness later in the day. Because the cultivar is generally positioned as evening cannabis, its later effects may be particularly appealing when productivity is no longer the priority.

Those potential uses should not be interpreted as evidence that the strain treats anxiety, chronic pain, insomnia, depression, or another medical condition. Dark Matter is a named cultivar rather than a standardized medication, and its cannabinoid chemistry changes between batches. High-THC marijuana can also worsen anxiety or cause uncomfortable impairment in susceptible individuals. Anyone using cannabis therapeutically should place more weight on the laboratory profile, dose, consumption method, personal tolerance, and professional medical guidance than on the reputation of the strain alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Dark Matter does not rely on one dominant flavor. Wizard Trees describes the flower as occupying a creamy, gassy, candy-sherb lane, and that description captures the basic framework well. Sweet fruit and candy appear first, but the profile soon becomes creamier and more floral. Apple-like brightness can emerge around the edges, followed by damp earth, black pepper, and fuel when the flowers are ground. Some batches lean heavily into perfume and sherbet, while others allow the gas and spice to become more prominent.

Laboratory testing gives the aroma a clearer chemical foundation. A November 2025 Dark Matter batch showed beta-caryophyllene at 0.998%, limonene at 0.380%, humulene at 0.223%, linalool at 0.171%, and fenchol at 0.111%, along with smaller amounts of terpineol, bisabolol, ocimene, and pinene. Another current retail batch lists beta-caryophyllene at 1.15%, limonene at 0.94%, linalool at 0.37%, myrcene at 0.30%, and humulene at 0.26%. Caryophyllene reinforces the peppery gas, limonene brightens the sweeter fruit, and linalool adds floral softness. On the palate, the sequence often moves from candy and cream toward spice, earth, and a persistent gassy finish.
Growing Information

Wizard Trees does not currently provide an official public cultivation sheet for Dark Matter, so precise flowering and yield figures should be treated more cautiously than the breeder-confirmed lineage. Third-party cultivation references commonly place indoor flowering around 56–63 days, or roughly eight to nine weeks. The plant is generally described as producing compact-to-medium growth with tightly stacked, heavily resinous flowers. Because the breeder’s finished flower consistently shows dense bud structure and substantial trichome coverage, airflow and late-flower humidity management deserve particular attention.

Indoor growers can benefit from creating an even canopy before the flowering stretch is complete. Topping, low-stress training, and selective pruning can improve light distribution without overcrowding the center of the plant. Dense flowers may require branch support toward maturity, particularly under strong lighting. Outdoors, the estimated flowering period suggests an early-to-mid-October harvest in many Northern Hemisphere environments, although local daylight patterns, phenotype, temperature, and autumn rainfall can shift maturity considerably.

Yield appears to be secondary to flower quality in the available descriptions. Rather than being promoted as a bulk-production cultivar, Dark Matter is distinguished by resin density, color, structure, and terpene complexity. Growers interested in preserving those qualities should pay close attention to drying and curing conditions after harvest. Excessive heat or overly rapid drying can remove the volatile floral, candy, and citrus compounds that separate this cultivar from more straightforward gas-heavy marijuana.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Dark Matter?

The Wizard Trees version of Dark Matter is Zoap × Y Life. Wizard Trees confirms this lineage directly on its official strain page. Other older strains named Dark Matter have different genetics, so the breeder should always be identified when researching this cultivar.
Is Dark Matter indica or sativa?

Wizard Trees markets Dark Matter as a hybrid with strong nighttime qualities. In practical terms, it behaves like an indica-leaning hybrid : cerebral and creative during the opening stage, then progressively heavier and more physically relaxing.
How strong is Dark Matter?

Potency varies significantly by harvest. Current Wizard Trees products have appeared from roughly 20% THC into the upper 20% range, including a batch listed at 28.76% THC. Consumers should use the laboratory result on the individual package rather than assuming a fixed percentage.
What does Dark Matter taste like?

The flavor combines sweet candy, creamy sherbet, floral notes, apple-like fruit, earth, peppery spice, and gas. Wizard Trees emphasizes the interaction between sweetness and fuel rather than one overpowering terpene note.
Is there more than one Dark Matter cannabis strain?

Yes. The name has been used by several breeders. Wizard Trees’ modern cultivar is Zoap × Y Life, while older Dark Matter strains from Kingdom Organic Seeds and North Genetics have entirely different pedigrees. The breeder name is therefore essential when comparing genetics.
Final Thoughts on Dark Matter

Dark Matter succeeds because it does not reduce modern exotic cannabis to potency and candy flavor alone. Zoap gives the hybrid floral sweetness, sherbet, and cream, while Y Life adds enough gas and structural depth to prevent the aroma from becoming predictable. The resulting weed moves between apple-like fruit, perfume, sugary cream, pepper, earth, and fuel, with laboratory results confirming a particularly strong contribution from beta-caryophyllene alongside limonene, linalool, humulene, and other supporting terpenes.

Its effects are equally layered. The experience begins upstairs, where creativity and cerebral engagement remain noticeable, but the body gradually catches up and changes the character of the high into something better suited to nighttime relaxation. Dense resinous flower and THC levels capable of approaching 29% add the potency expected from Wizard Trees genetics without becoming the cultivar’s only selling point. Most importantly, anyone adding Dark Matter to a strain library should identify it specifically as the Wizard Trees Zoap × Y Life version. With several unrelated cultivars carrying the same name, that distinction preserves the genetic accuracy that a serious cannabis reference should provide.
